question: Does spatial ofer admit accusative/dative government, beyond the case-syncretic Creation eorðan and Cook glossary gloss?
finding: Yes. The registered Fulk2020 text explicitly lists ofer in§36 among the accusative/dative prepositions. Its glossary independently encodes the same fact through the defined obelus. All three page images have been inspected.
scope_recommendation: A bounded spatial ofer sense can be taught with this reference; local Creation ofer eorðan remains case-syncretic, so do not require a unique case label there. Authority ofer+acc remains a separate source-supported productive frame. Broader temporal, degree, adversative, causative-emotion and discourse senses remain unassigned.
proposed_learner_rule: Spatial ofer means over/across and may govern accusative or dative. The construction and meaning guide the case. In ofer eorðan, the noun form itself does not distinguish the two cases.
source_limits: Cook307 only glosses ofer; it does not explicitly demonstrate both governments.
Cook166/172 are general preposition rules and do not name ofer.
The prior course online dictionary note was a lead, not facsimile proof; it was not reused as sufficient evidence.
Fulk§36 states a general tendency, not an exceptionless rule or free interchangeability of cases in every phrase.
